fact: A colossal red supergiant marking Orion's shoulder — so large it would swallow the inner planets if placed at the Sun.
bio: Betelgeuse (Alpha Orionis) is a semiregular variable near the end of its life. Estimates place it several hundred light-years away with large uncertainty. It will one day end as a supernova — briefly rivalling the Moon in our sky.
cultural: Its dramatic dimming in 2019–2020 (a dust cloud, not imminent collapse) drew worldwide attention. The name descends from Arabic, and the star features across countless sky-lore traditions as a shoulder or hand of the hunter.
